title: Preservability of Measurement Incompatibility: Purification, Activation, and a No-Go Theorem
authors: Chao-Hsien Wu, Franco Nori, Huan-Yu Ku
abstract: Measurement incompatibility is a fundamental quantum resource that enables advantages in many quantum information tasks, including cryptography and communication. However, unavoidable interactions between a system and its environment can degrade or even completely destroy measurement incompatibility; such a process is referred to as a measurement-incompatibility-annihilating channel. Recently, the capability of noisy quantum dynamics to preserve measurement incompatibility has been characterized within the resource theory of measurement incompatibility preservability. This motivates studying how to purify the preservation of measurement incompatibility and how to activate it from a measurement-incompatibility-annihilating channel. To this end, we first introduce our figures of merit as robustness-based resource monotones within this resource theory. We demonstrate that while pre-filtering operations can strengthen measurement incompatibility preservability, they cannot activate it from an incompatibility-annihilating channel, establishing a no-go theorem. Furthermore, we explicitly demonstrate that an incompatibility-annihilating channel can be stochastically activated via post-filtering operations. Our results provide a practical framework for exploiting measurement incompatibility in quantum information processing.
summary: This work develops a resource theory to quantify measurement incompatibility preservability under noise. The authors prove that while noise can destroy this resource, they establish a no-go theorem against pre-filtering recovery but show that post-filtering can successfully activate the resource. This provides a practical guide for exploiting incompatibility in quantum information protocols.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental quantum resource of measurement incompatibility and how its preservation degrades under noisy quantum channels.
main_result: They establish a no-go theorem showing pre-filtering cannot activate incompatibility, but demonstrate that post-filtering can stochastically activate such channels.
method: The authors develop a resource theory framework, introducing robustness-based monotones, and utilize semidefinite programming (SDP) and iterative algorithms (seesaw) to quantify these properties.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum channels ($\mathcal{N}$) acting on quantum systems, characterized by measurement assemblages ($\{M_a\}_{a,x}$), and the concept of measurement incompatibility.
key_observables: Measurement Incompatibility, Resource Monotone $R_{	ext{JIMIP}}(\mathcal{N})$, Quantum Steerability.
important_parameters: Noise strength ($t$), channel parameters (e.g., amplitude damping parameter $p$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on reformulating the resource measure using the Choi–Jamiolkowski isomorphism and assuming the equivalence between steering and measurement incompatibility.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schemes for IA channels and numerically compare the preservation/activation of incompatibility using pre-filter only, post-filter only, and combined pre-post-filter operations.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the resource theory, defines the monotone $R_{	ext{JIMIP}}$, proves its properties (Faithfulness, Monotonicity), establishes the no-go theorem for pre-filtering, and finally demonstrates activation via post-filtering.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, quantitative framework (resource theory) for understanding how fundamental quantum correlations, like measurement incompatibility, are degraded by noise and how they might be recovered or utilized.
